findings.where: spec §9 'The branch rule' rule 1 (lines 6061-6066); X0.2 row; P-112 (d) 'Where a reset session resumes after X7.1' (spec line 1027); record §P 'Rulings' P-112 (d)
findings.problem: The only test for 'the execution PR has merged' is a commit subject: 'main holds a merged `closeout-residuals X6.4:` commit'. After a merged failure record, the test is 'a merged `closeout-residuals record: X7.<s> failed`'. This repository squash-merges every PR, and P-83 itself says 'the squash merge'. A squash leaves no commit with that subject on main; the subjects survive only as '* …' lines in the squash body, and only under the current GitHub message setting. The test is therefore not mechanical, and read as a subject test it is false. A session after X7.1 then misses the merge and starts at X0.2. X0.3(a) finds the registry at 97bda1a0… instead of 8b4e46ed… and stops. Stop step 1 reads the merged EX/ctrl/sent.txt, which lists TRACK-FREEZE-START, and sets past_x50 true. The stop record then files 'attempt 1 stopped at X0.3' and writes TRACK-UNIT-STOPPED and TRACK-STATUS-STOP-01..03 on the tracking page, for a unit that passed and merged. This is the exact resume case P-112 (d) was added for.
findings.evidence: Every recent commit on main is a squash commit titled '<PR title> (#NNN)', for example 77d98dd and d848942. For the branch subject 'docs(ephemeral): modification intake - Alpha Feedback open entries', `git log origin/main --format=%s | grep -c '^docs(ephemeral): modification intake - Alpha Feedback open entries'` gives 0, while `git log origin/main --grep=…` finds d848942 through its body. P-83 (spec line 384) says the lease is needed 'because the squash merge leaves the remote branch's old history in place'. X0.3(a) pins the registry at 8b4e46ed…, but after X7.1 main holds 97bda1a0… (§8.6). Per the §9 'A failing gate' bullet, a failing gate before X5.0 runs stop step 1, whose past_x50 comes from EX/ctrl/sent.txt.
findings.fix: Base the test on content, not subjects. 'The execution PR has merged' becomes `git cat-file -e origin/main:docs/ephemeral/modifications/evidence/closeout-residuals/execute/run.json` together with main's record reading `status: EXECUTING`. EX reaches main only through the execution PR, because every stop record moves it to AT. For a merged failure record, have the failure-record commit add a key to EX/run.json (`runjson.py EX/run.json failed_X7.<s> <date>`) and test that key on origin/main. If a grep is kept instead, state the exact command: `git log origin/main --grep='^\* closeout-residuals X6.4:'`. Also add to X0.2 a refusal when origin/main already holds EX/run.json, so a missed detection can never enter the stop path.

findings.problem: X6.4's path check is `git diff --name-only origin/main HEAD`, a two-dot diff between trees. Every push first runs `git fetch --prune`, so origin/main is fresh. Any commit that lands on main between X0.2 and X6.4 outside the three open paths therefore appears in the list, and the check fails. PF10 build-notes updates are one example: they are committed straight to main, as in 3b8084d. Past X5.0 a failing X6.4 gate stops the unit. The whole landed unit is then swept and reversed, the new page is trashed, and Nathan must restore 50 bodies from page history, all because of an unrelated commit that does not stop the execution PR from merging. The freeze stops flow sessions only, not other commits to main, and X0.2 to X6.4 spans the D24 review and the landing, easily a day.

Commit 3b8084d ('PF10 update build notes to v13.2.9') on main has no PR number, showing that direct commits to main happen. Nothing in the spec handles main moving (grep for 'origin/main...', 'merge-base' and 'main moved' finds nothing).
findings.fix: Compare against the recorded base or the merge base: `git diff --name-only "$(python3 -c 'import json;print(json.load(open("EX/run.json"))["base"])')" HEAD` or `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD`. findings.problem: After X7.1, where a reset session resumes depends on whether 'main holds a merged `closeout-residuals X6.4:` commit' and 'a merged `closeout-residuals record: X7.<s> failed`'. This repository squash-merges its PRs, and the plan itself says so (spec line 384: 'because the squash merge leaves the remote…'). A squash merge leaves no commit with that subject on main: the subject becomes the PR title, and the branch's subjects appear only as '* …' bullet lines in the squash commit's body. No command is given for this test. Checked literally against subjects, it finds nothing, so rule 1 falls through to its default, starting at X0.2. That default would re-run the whole of EXECUTE after the unit has merged, and after X7.3 X0.3(b) would then fail on the installed skills and trigger a stop record. X7.2, X7.4 and every post-merge session depend on this test.

In my scratch remote I squash-merged a branch whose tip was 'closeout-residuals X6.4: execution record' the way GitHub does. `git log --format=%s origin/main | grep -c '^closeout-residuals X6.4:'` printed 0, `git log --grep='closeout-residuals X6.4:'` found 1 (the body bullet), and the branch rule took rule 1 (reset).
findings.fix: Give the test as a command that holds under squash merges. Robust option: EX/ reaches main only through the execution PR (a stop record moves EX to AT/execute), so test `git cat-file -e origin/main:docs/ephemeral/modifications/evidence/closeout-residuals/execute/graph_check.json` (X6.4 commits EX/graph_check.json) for 'the execution PR has merged'. Detect a merged failure record the same way, e.g. by §E's 'X7.<s> failed' row on main's record, or by `git log origin/main --format=%B | grep -q '^\* closeout-residuals record: X7\.[0-9] failed'`.
